sources.entry: tubesync ⚠ - Syncs YouTube channels and playlists to a locally hosted media server. AGPL-3.0 Docker/Python

summary.one_liner: TubeSync is a self-hosted PVR for YouTube that syncs channels and playlists to local directories and updates Plex or Jellyfin when media is downloaded.
summary.what_it_does: TubeSync is a web interface wrapper around yt-dlp and ffmpeg with a built-in task scheduler. You add YouTube channels or playlists as sources, choose an index frequency and media quality, and it periodically indexes them and downloads new media. Audio-only media goes to an audio directory and media with video goes to a video directory under the download path. It retries failed downloads with back-off timers over an extended period. It can notify a local Jellyfin or Plex media server once media is downloaded. All administration is done through the web interface.
use_cases: Automatically download new videos from YouTube channels
Archive YouTube playlists to a local media library
Feed downloaded YouTube videos into Jellyfin or Plex
Choose video quality and formats for YouTube downloads
Self-hosted alternative to a Sonarr-style workflow for YouTube
how_to_run: docker run -d --name tubesync -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 -e TZ=Europe/London -v /some/directory/tubesync-config:/config -v /some/directory/tubesync-downloads:/downloads -p 4848:4848 --stop-timeout 1800 ghcr.io/meeb/tubesync:latest
Open http://localhost:4848 in a browser to reach the dashboard and add sources
notable: Full PVR workflow with automatic updates to Plex and Jellyfin media servers
Gradual retry of failed downloads with back-off timers
Runs in Docker or Podman on amd64 and arm64
Config, thumbnails and SQLite database kept in one /config directory for easy backup and migration
Optional HTTP basic auth and external database support
caveats: Indexing very large channels on short intervals can keep the instance busy without downloading media, and may get the IP throttled or banned by the source
Media server integration is limited to Plex and Jellyfin
Logging, advanced guides and FAQ are on the wiki rather than in the README
